items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: I said, well “You booked The Big Four.” He was our manager/agent.

ctx.x: Well Red Norvo was getting more work because of Louis.

Oh well I don’t mean especially Red Norvo. He came to mind because he’s the reason why I went with Louis. Not especially but when Joe Glaser called me, the first time he called me to go with Louis, it’s a funny story because he said, “Marty this is Joe Glaser. Did you work with Phil Napoleon’s Memphis Five?” I said, “yeah, why?” He said, “you play Dixieland?” I said, “I guess so, if I worked with Phil’s band I guess.” He said, “well you want to go with Louis Armstrong?” And I said, “no.” He said, “did you hear…

The Big Four. We went to Chicago for two weeks and we stayed four months and my wife was ready to jump off a bridge. And so was I, I mean I was away so long. So I made a promise to her I said okay that’s it, I’m not going on the road anymore. So he says, “Are you crazy?” He said, “look at what happened with Earl Hines.” Earl had a big name but not as big as Louis. But when he went with Louis, they were equal and he was getting like equal publicity and stuff. Even though Louis was the boss, but Earl, it got him…
